Nestlé opens Orbe Deep Tech Centre to pilot AI and robotics

The Swiss centre initially brings together about 60 staff to test technologies before wider factory deployment.

SWI swissinfo.ch / Keystone-SDA ↗20 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

The new development

Nestlé has opened a Deep Tech Centre in Orbe, Switzerland, according to November 20 reporting. It initially brings together about 60 staff and works with partners including Microsoft and Boston Dynamics. The centre provides a place to develop and test technologies before deciding how to expand their practical use.

Technology and applications

Its remit includes AI, smart sensors and robotics across product development and manufacturing. Factory applications aim to improve quality checks and process efficiency while reducing repetitive or physically demanding work. Technologies will first be tested in Orbe pilot plants before potential deployment elsewhere in the company.

Scope and next steps

The centre complements a technology hub in Shenzhen. The announcement does not provide a worldwide robot-installation count or demonstrated cost savings. It represents additional capacity for experimentation and validation, rather than proof that every project is commercially ready or has already generated financial returns.
